title: The History of Mor Dimet, the Prince of Diyarbakır
source_text:
Kaleyo Mar Duməṭ, hawi qadišo, u+abro du+šulṭònowa.
Qṭəlle ann+armnoye kulle. 
D ʔArzrum, qṭəlle ann+armnoye kulle. 
Lu+aġaṯṯe qṭilile, lo+kuḏʕono əšme mənyo.
Də Ṣṭambəl ... ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥̚ qṭile də Ṣṭambəl ann+armnoye kulle.
ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥̚ hawo, kuḏʕono əšme. 
Də Dyarbákərste lo+kuḏʕono əšme. 
Mbele šwaʕmo+zlamat armnoye ʕal u+pər dә Dyarbakər, nḥərre aš+šawʕo … šwaʕmo.
Ŭ daʕiri ʕal i+qriṯo, ay+yasire, an+naʕime, ax+xətyàr d̥xoṯi, qṭilənne.
Ŭ aǧ+ǧehəl, ak̇+k̇ačk̇at, hak̇a bgawre, ŭ hak̇a ṭlibe, mnayšne, ŭ hak̇a k̇aččək̇at, mhirənne bu+zōr, mhirənne. 
U+abro du+šulṭono dә Dyarbakər qorewa bə Ṣṭambəl. 
Qorewa bə Ṣṭambəl Maktab̥, ṭălăbá, ṭălăbá du+maktab̥. 
Yawmo ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥̚ komar, ‘Šaməʕno d̥fāš ḥappoṯe d̥ṣuroye bә Dyarbakər. 
Lázəmyo dməqšoʕi!’
U+abro du+šulṭono dә Diyarbakər mqadamle, məḷḷe, ‘Ya ṣəlṭán, ono koḏaʕno, ono u+abro du+šulṭono dә Diyarbákərno. 
Koḏaʕno am+maġarat daṣ+ṣuroye áykone. 
U+ḥa d̥fā́šәste, dobatli ʕaskar, g̊ˠqoṭanne.
E, ánnaqqa ṣə́dlele qadr omar, ‘Ṣafro, betfā́q, mbal aṭ+ṭằlăba du+maktab̥ kulle ʕam ruḥux ŭ ḥa lo+ṭorat!’
Qayəm, ŭ lə+ṭrele dəzze lutel, ŭ húlele ḥšamto basəmto. 
Húlele ḥšamto basəmto ŭ madmaxle gab ruḥe, bi+oda … boda+ḥreto. 
Húlele oda naḏəfto.
Ŭ damixi. 
Damixi, aṯi malaxo Gabriʔél mi+šmayo.
Naḥət ʕal ṣadre. 
Omar, ‘U+ḥa d̥fāš me qmu+sayfo dbabux, quṭlaṭle? 
At+tarte+ʕaynayḏux gmofáqnanne’.
Səmle lo+səmle, omar, ‘Əlláh gmofaqno ʕaynux’. 
Ŭ lúlele darbo dmofaq ʕayne, ḥəngi mlaʕe ebe, omar, ‘ʕAyni lo+məfqatte. 
U+mede d̥kəbʕat, səm ebi!’
Hăma brəmle u+garmo du+maġàz, dʕarquwe. 
Brəmle hawxa, ŭ ha, u+garmano du+maġàz, dʕarquwe, ha hano brəmle, hawxa səmle.
Nafəl k̇arăk̇ā́r aʕle, ŭ saləq li+šmayo. 
Omar, ‘U+ḥa d̥fāš me qmu+sayfo dbabux, quṭlaṭle?’
‘K̇ār ŭ k̇ār ŭ āy ŭ āy ŭ āy’. 
Qolo bi+arʕo, ḥa bi+šmayo.
Ánnaqqa, e, mə‿g̊soyam? 
Konofaq, harke lə+ksōm idara. 
Nafəq lu+ṣalòn, kuzzé ŭ oṯe, lә+ksōm idara.
Azzeyo, nafəq lu+balqòn, lə+ksōm idara. 
K̇ār ŭ k̇ar, hul nafəq ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥, maḥəsle ʕal qole.
‘He, abro, mə‿xēryo?’ 
Omar, ‘Ḥāl ŭ măsale. 
Ašə́r aṯili malaxo Gabriʔél’.
Mə́ḷḷeli, ‘Ay+yasire d̥fayiši me qmu+sayfo dbabux, ʕaynux ʕal d̥quṭlatte, qušʕátteyo? 
At+tarte+ʕaynayḏux gmaṭə́ṇṇanne!’
Lə+ṭreli maṭər ʕayni, ašə́r grəšle u+garmo du+maġàz, qṭíleli, idara lə+ksōmno. 
ṣəlṭán Ḥamíd̥ madʕaḷḷe aʕle, məḷḷe, ‘Čara latlux! 
Lo ono kə́tlilux čara ŭ lo at+taxetər kətlux čara. 
Lázəmyo dəzzúx qəm ʕito daṣ+ṣuroye, quṭʕat tawbe. 
Zux, mḥalqat ruḥux ltor ŭ baxt dʕito mdaṣ+ṣuroye. 
Hăk̇a nāḥlux … naxwa ašə́r čara latlux. 
Taxetər, čara layt’.
Qām azzeyo, zangīnwa. 
Mbele kallawat ġắlăbe ŭ səmle muklo, ʕazima li+ʕito d Urfa.
Mḥalaqle ruḥe ltōr ŭ baxt di+ʕito d Urfa, ŭ səmle muklone basime, ŭ mʕazamle i+walaye kula, ŭ daməx bgawa di+ʕito du+qadišo, ŭ húlele kallawat ġắlăbe lu+qadišo.
I+brusk̇e nayiḥo, i+brusk̇e nayiḥo. 
Eló balé ṣắqaṭyo, ṣắqaṭyo, komaʕraǧ bәḥḏo+raġlo.
Məḷḷe, ‘Bəṯr dǧarili hawxa, ono haw kosōmno aġatiye, ṣəlṭaniye! 
Ono g̊d̥oweno dayroyo, ʕabodo, g̊ˠqoreno, g̊d̥oweno mšiḥoyo’.
Məthaymalle bә Mšiḥo ŭ hawi dayroyo, hawi ʕabodo. 
Hawi qadišo. 
Kalayo uʕdo i+ʕito d Zāz, ʕal ə́šmeyo, Mar Duməṭ.
Mar Duməṭ kalayo b Zāz. 
Hayo ʕal ə́šmeyo. 
Háyostene ... hūn … d̥owutu šani sāġ, háwoste kamilo, hawxa.

sentences.source_line: Zux, mḥalqat ruḥux ltor ŭ baxt dʕito mdaṣ+ṣuroye.
sentences.translation: Go, you’ll throw yourself to the mercy (lit. ‘protection and honor’) of one of the Christian churches (lit. ‘a church from one of the Christians’).

items.value: Zux, mḥalqat ruḥux ltor ŭ baxt dʕito mdaṣ+ṣuroye.
Go, you’ll throw yourself to the mercy (lit. ‘protection and honor’) of one of the Christian churches (lit. ‘a church from one of the Christians’).

sentences.source_line: Hăk̇a nāḥlux … naxwa ašə́r čara latlux.
sentences.translation: If you get well … (great), otherwise, surely nothing can help you (lit. ‘there’s no cure for you’).

items.value: Hăk̇a nāḥlux … naxwa ašə́r čara latlux.
If you get well … (great), otherwise, surely nothing can help you (lit. ‘there’s no cure for you’).

sentences.source_line: Taxetər, čara layt’.
sentences.translation: Doctors, there’s no cure’.

sentences.source_line: Qām azzeyo, zangīnwa.
sentences.translation: He up and went, he was rich.

items.value: He up and went, he was rich.

sentences.source_line: Mbele kallawat ġắlăbe ŭ səmle muklo, ʕazima li+ʕito d Urfa.
sentences.translation: He brought a lot of money and made a meal, a banquet for the church of Urfa.

items.value: Mbele kallawat ġắlăbe ŭ səmle muklo, ʕazima li+ʕito d Urfa.
He brought a lot of money and made a meal, a banquet for the church of Urfa.

sentences.source_line: Mḥalaqle ruḥe ltōr ŭ baxt di+ʕito d Urfa, ŭ səmle muklone basime, ŭ mʕazamle i+walaye kula, ŭ daməx bgawa di+ʕito du+qadišo, ŭ húlele kallawat ġắlăbe lu+qadišo.
sentences.translation: He threw himself to the mercy (lit. ‘protection and honor’) of the church of Urfa, and made nice dishes, invited the whole city, slept inside the church of that saint, and gave a lot of money to the saint.

items.value: Mḥalaqle ruḥe ltōr ŭ baxt di+ʕito d Urfa, ŭ səmle muklone basime, ŭ mʕazamle i+walaye kula, ŭ daməx bgawa di+ʕito du+qadišo, ŭ húlele kallawat ġắlăbe lu+qadišo.

He threw himself to the mercy (lit. ‘protection and honor’) of the church of Urfa, and made nice dishes, invited the whole city, slept inside the church of that saint, and gave a lot of money to the saint.

sentences.source_line: I+brusk̇e nayiḥo, i+brusk̇e nayiḥo.
sentences.translation: The pain got better, the pain got better.

items.value: The pain got better, the pain got better.

sentences.source_line: Eló balé ṣắqaṭyo, ṣắqaṭyo, komaʕraǧ bәḥḏo+raġlo.
sentences.translation: But he is lame, he is lame, he is limping on one leg.

items.value: Eló balé ṣắqaṭyo, ṣắqaṭyo, komaʕraǧ bәḥḏo+raġlo.
But he is lame, he is lame, he is limping on one leg.

sentences.source_line: Məḷḷe, ‘Bəṯr dǧarili hawxa, ono haw kosōmno aġatiye, ṣəlṭaniye!
sentences.translation: He said, ‘After this happened to me, I’ll no longer act as agha, sultan (lit. ‘do aghahood, sultanhood’)!

items.value: Məḷḷe, ‘Bəṯr dǧarili hawxa, ono haw kosōmno aġatiye, ṣəlṭaniye!
He said, ‘After this happened to me, I’ll no longer act as agha, sultan (lit. ‘do aghahood, sultanhood’)!

sentences.source_line: Ono g̊d̥oweno dayroyo, ʕabodo, g̊ˠqoreno, g̊d̥oweno mšiḥoyo’.
sentences.translation: I’ll become a monk, a worshipper, I’ll study, I’ll become a Christian’.

items.value: Ono g̊d̥oweno dayroyo, ʕabodo, g̊ˠqoreno, g̊d̥oweno mšiḥoyo’.
I’ll become a monk, a worshipper, I’ll study, I’ll become a Christian’.

sentences.source_line: Məthaymalle bә Mšiḥo ŭ hawi dayroyo, hawi ʕabodo.
sentences.translation: He came to believe in Christ and he became a monk, a worshipper.

items.value: Məthaymalle bә Mšiḥo ŭ hawi dayroyo, hawi ʕabodo.
He came to believe in Christ and he became a monk, a worshipper.

sentences.source_line: Hawi qadišo.
sentences.translation: He became a saint.

sentences.source_line: Kalayo uʕdo i+ʕito d Zāz, ʕal ə́šmeyo, Mar Duməṭ.
sentences.translation: Now there’s the church in Zaz, it’s in his name, St Dometius.

items.value: Kalayo uʕdo i+ʕito d Zāz, ʕal ə́šmeyo, Mar Duməṭ.
Now there’s the church in Zaz, it’s in his name, St Dometius.

sentences.source_line: Mar Duməṭ kalayo b Zāz.
sentences.translation: St Dometius, here it is in Zaz.

items.value: St Dometius, here it is in Zaz.

sentences.source_line: Hayo ʕal ə́šmeyo.
sentences.translation: That one’s in his name.

sentences.source_line: Háyostene ... hūn … d̥owutu šani sāġ, háwoste kamilo, hawxa.
sentences.translation: That one too… you … you be well for me, that one is finished, like so.

items.value: Háyostene ... hūn … d̥owutu šani sāġ, háwoste kamilo, hawxa.
That one too… you … you be well for me, that one is finished, like so.
